threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think a '5-minute stroll' means a straight line to the pub, not a detour through three pop-up coffee shops and a market.
Caught a bloke in a three-piece suit arguing with a tree at the bus stop last night. Felt like I was in a surreal play, but he seemed dead serious.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing the late-night kebab orders mixing with the sound of street musicians, I realized Berlin's heartbeat is just outside my window.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do they turn a street party into a pop-up park; they bring in real grass, benches, and DJ decks. It's like a mini-festival for a weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to a BART delay—most just sigh and roll their eyes, while newcomers start looking for rideshare apps.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Last week, saw a guy serenading the Muni crowd with an old guitar, while a raccoon rummaged through a trash can nearby. Classic SF vibe.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think plaça del Sol is just for sunbathing, but locals use it for evening hangouts and impromptu concerts. Totally different vibe.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at how cut-off the metro is during major events. That deer-in-headlights look by the travel maps says it all.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest tube instead of knowing the bus routes. It's all about the bus here, mate.
Caught a guy dancing in the aisle on the 63 last night, completely oblivious to the stares. Ah, Peckham on a Saturday.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw an old lady feeding pigeons while debating politics with a street artist. Only in Neukölln do arguments feel like community events.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find currywurst trucks and art galleries side by side, soaking up street art while grabbing a bite at 3 AM.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a tourist when they stop to gawk at the murals but locals know to keep moving—painted walls won’t save you from a BART delay.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 14 Mission arguing with a pigeon over a discarded burrito. The bird won. Classic SF moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just one big party, but they miss the quiet afternoons when locals sip vermut and catch up at the plaza.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stand in the middle of the street, staring at their phone maps, completely oblivious to the flow of pedestrians.
